title: Aster Logistics outbound playbook scratchpad
content:
Quick notes / hypothesis (raw):
- Aster Logistics (Aster) is a mid-size 3PL focusing on refrigerated freight across EU + UK and recently launched a US-Europe cross-dock program. They care about predictability and regulatory data isolation (GDPR, some UK-specific regs).
- Pain: spikes in routing/planning calls -> unpredictable token costs on homegrown LLM; operational alerts have noisy false positives; they want <100ms steady-state latency for critical routing decisions.
- Why Redwood might be interesting: predictable dedicated capacity (Reserved) + private deployment (VPC) for GDPR, plus Optimize to lower per-token costs and suggestions for quantization/batching. Also rollouts + automatic fallback are attractive for reliability during peak season.

Account background (raw research):
- Founded 2014; HQ Rotterdam; ~520 employees; revenue ~€120M (YC/Crunch notes).
- Tech stack: Node + Python microservices, Postgres, Kafka. Has a TMS (Transport Management System) built in-house with APIs.
- Reported pain: planning system slows at 20k requests/min during peak; caching not implemented for AI-derived scoring.
- Security/regulatory: data residency required for EU customer PII; procurement requires at least ISO27001 + SOC2 (they asked for SOC2 in RFP).

Key stakeholders (names pulled from LinkedIn / SFDC):
- Head of Product: Sander de Vries (Lead for TMS modernization) — influencer, cares latency/costs
- VP Ops: Claire O'Neill — cares reliability, SLA, uptime across peak seasons
- Director of Security/Compliance: Martin K. — will push for Private or Dedicated with KMS/HSM integration
- Procurement: Rajiv Malhotra — will try to push lowest cost multi-vendor approach; timeline Q1 procurement cycle (starts mid-Feb)

Initial thesis for approach:
- Start with a small Dedicated pilot for routing scoring: reserve a predictable pool sized for their 20k req/min pattern (we can propose burst capacity for seasonal peaks).
- Offer a Private (VPC) eval for compliance show-and-tell (demo with KMS integration and EU-only regions).
- Focus messaging on: predictable per-token economics, latency SLOs, and rollouts/fallback.

Potential objections and suggested counters (brain dump):
- "We can host ourselves" -> Counter: True, but we do the heavy lifting on performance tuning (kernel selection, batching, KV cache) and we expose predictable cost controls + SLA so your platform team can avoid building and maintaining inference stack. Offer cost comparison matrix vs. self-hosting 6/12/24 months (I should draft).
- "Security/PII concerns" -> Counter: Private deployment with customer-controlled VPC and KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 + ISO info pack. Offer a short security runbook and customer checklist.
- "Price is high" -> Counter: Show Optimize features (batching, caching) and model/quantization recommendations that typically reduce per-token cost by 30-60%. Show case study: Retail partner saved 42% on inference costs after Optimize. Present pilot pricing (fixed commit + performance review).
- "Vendor lock" -> Counter: Emphasize open model support and easy export/rollback. Demonstrate how rollouts and pinned model versions make migration out/in less risky.

Outbound sequence (short):
1) Email 1 (value): 1-2 lines calling out routing latency + cost predictability. Attach short one-pager (POC idea).
2) Email 2 (social proof): callout retail/3PL example with numbers; ask for intro to Sander / Claire.
3) LinkedIn + SFDC touch (message to Sander + brief note to Claire).
4) If no response, send pilot offer w/ pricing (3-week pilot, limited to routing-scoring microservice, Redwood provides infra and tuning).

Sample subject / opening lines (scratch):
- Subject: "Cut routing latency spikes — pilot proposal for Aster Logistics"
- Opening line: "Sander — quick note: we helped a 3PL cut routing decision latency 2.5x while reducing per-request cost by ~40%. Would love to propose the same formula for Aster in a short pilot."

POC idea (technical):
- Scope: Replace scoring endpoint for lane selection (single microservice) with Redwood-hosted inference. Keep existing TMS logic; Redwood returns scores + top-3 explanations for audit.
- Success metrics: median latency <100ms for 95% of requests, peak throughput support up to 25k rps (for one region), cost per 1M evaluations < €X (need to compute), improved match quality (ops KPI) by X% (ops to define).
- Duration: 3 weeks (2 weeks integration + 1 week load run + review).
- Deliverables: infra config, security checklist, runbook, dashboard access (Console), cost/latency report.

Technical notes to engineering contact (for intro):
- Need ability to route scoring calls to Redwood: POST /score {shipment, constraints}. Prefer gRPC but can do REST.
- Provide sample payload sizes (avg 2k tokens per request? check with them). If large sequences, suggest quantization profile and KV-prefix caching to reduce work.
- Ask for: representative payloads, peak QPS windows, retention requirements for logs, and whether they can sanitize PII for pilot.

Open questions (todo / research):
- Confirm average token count per scoring call (estimate: 500–2,000 tokens).
- Get concrete uptime/SLA target from Claire. Is 99.95% baseline acceptable?
- Procurement windows — confirm Rajiv's internal timelines. He mentioned mid-Feb start (need verified).
- Which EU region do they prefer? NL-FRA-IE?
- Any existing vendor relationships (Google Vertex/Anthropic) to position against? Check SFDC notes.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: They insist on full on-prem airgapped install -> Mitigate: offer private deployment + on-prem package (but will need eng resource estimate and pricing delta).
- Risk: They want lower price than pilot economics -> Mitigate: propose trial with usage cap and phased committed capacity after success.

Next steps (action list):
- [ ] Draft 1-pager POC and cost estimate (Maya) — due 2026-03-14 (align to procurement window).
- [ ] Attach SOC2/ISO pack + security runbook (SSO/KMS slides) (Jonah).
- [ ] Quick internal sync with Solutions Eng to size Dedicated pilot (Priya) — include GPU type, burst policy, and observability hooks.
- [ ] Build outbound email (2 variants) and test subject lines (split test).
- [ ] Pull SFDC notes and confirm stakeholder emails / phone numbers (Maya).

Call prep script (50–60s opening + probing):
- Opening: "Hi Sander — thanks for taking a quick call. I want to focus on one measurable win: eliminating routing latency spikes while keeping costs predictable. Can I run a quick hypothesis and get your reaction?"
- Probing: "How do you currently score routes? What's the typical payload/size? Where are you seeing the biggest latency/cost pain?"
- Security probe: "Do you have constraints around where inference runs or key management?"
- Close: "If this looks promising I can lay out a 3-week pilot we can run with your TMS team — minimal changes, clear success metrics."

Notes-to-self style reminders: short, choppy allowed —
- Keep POC scope tiny: one microservice, no data model changes.
- Emphasize cost predictability up front (they hate surprises).
- Use EU-region talk track and Private deployment to get past security guard.
- Bring up fallback policies: Redwood can automatically route to lower-cost model if load spikes. Good selling point for Claire.

Possible sales motion options (ranked):
1) Direct Dedicated pilot (fastest to show latency/cost) -> convert to reserved commit.
2) Private VPC trial (if compliance blocks Dedicated) -> longer procurement but closes security reqs.
3) On-prem eval (last resort) -> expensive and slow.

Metrics to include in follow-up one-pager (must collect from them):
- Current median/95th latency for scoring endpoint
- Current cost/pricing for existing AI calls (if possible) or ops estimate
- Peak and baseline QPS windows by region
- Ops KPI tied to scoring quality (failures, misroutes, exceptions)

Slack drafts (for quick internal pings):
- To Jonah: "Hey — can you pull SOC2 pack + short summary slides? Aster Logistics prepping procurement in mid-Feb, want to attach to pilot doc."
- To Priya: "Need Dedicated sizing: 25k rps peak, mostly eu-west. Can you sketch GPU & pool suggestion + burst?"

End of scratchpad. Keep this lean and iterative — will evolve after first call.
